Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the maximum amount of 'Leave Not Due' (LND) that can be granted to a Government servant during their entire service career?
Brief_Explanation: Rule 31 of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972 states that 'Leave Not Due' shall be limited to a maximum of 360 days during the entire service, which shall be debited against the half pay leave the Government servant may earn subsequently.

Question_Text: As per the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, a Government servant belonging to Group 'A' or Group 'B' must report to the Government any transaction in movable property if the value of such property exceeds:
Option_A: Two months' basic pay of the Government servant
Option_B: One month's basic pay of the Government servant
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 18(3) of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, a Government servant must report any transaction in movable property if its value exceeds two months' basic pay (for Group A and B) or one month's basic pay (for Group C and D).

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, which kind of leave is NOT debited to the leave account of a Government servant?
Brief_Explanation: Maternity Leave, Paternity Leave, and Child Care Leave are specialized leaves and are not debited to the regular running leave account of a Government servant.

Question_Text: What is the maximum period of continuous Half Pay Leave (HPL) that can be granted to a Government servant under normal circumstances?
Option_D: No such ceiling exists, subject only to availability at credit
Brief_Explanation: Unlike Earned Leave, which is capped at 180 days at a time, there is no maximum limit for the amount of Half Pay Leave (HPL) that can be granted at one time, subject only to the balance available at credit.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, which of the following is considered as 'Speculation' in stock, share, or other investments?
Option_B: Frequent purchase and sale of shares, securities, or other investments
Brief_Explanation: Rule 16 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 states that frequent purchase or sale of shares, securities, or other investments shall be deemed to be speculation, which is prohibited.

Question_Text: As per the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the maximum number of days of Earned Leave (EL) that can be credited in advance to a Government servant's account on 1st January and 1st July every year?
Brief_Explanation: Earned Leave is credited in advance at the rate of 15 days on the 1st of January and 15 days on the 1st of July each year, totaling 30 days in a calendar year.

Question_Text: If a female Government servant legally adopts a child below the age of one year, she is entitled to Child Adoption Leave for a maximum period of:
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 43-B of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, a female Government servant with fewer than two surviving children who legally adopts a child below one year is eligible for Child Adoption Leave for 180 days.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, what is the financial limit above which a gift received from near relatives on ceremonial occasions must be reported to the Government by a Group 'C' official?
Brief_Explanation: According to the updated Rule 13 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, Group C officials must report gifts from near relatives if the value exceeds Rs. 7,500 (for Group A and B, the limit is Rs. 25,000).

Question_Text: An official under suspension is entitled to which of the following allowances during the suspension period?
Option_B: Subsistence allowance equal to half pay leave salary and dearness allowance
Option_C: Subsistence allowance equal to earned leave salary and DA
Option_D: No allowance is paid during suspension
Brief_Explanation: Under Fundamental Rule 53, an official under suspension is entitled to a subsistence allowance equal to the leave salary which the officer would have drawn if on half-pay leave, plus dearness allowance.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, which of the following is correct regarding 'Commuted Leave'?
Option_A: It can only be granted on a medical certificate.
Option_B: It is debited at double the rate against the half pay leave account.
Option_C: It is credited in advance at the rate of 15 days every half-year.
Option_D: It can be claimed as a matter of right.
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 30, Commuted Leave is debited against the half pay leave account at double the rate of the leave taken (e.g., 10 days of commuted leave debits 20 days of HPL).

Question_Text: What is the maximum limit of 'Extraordinary Leave' (EOL) that can be granted to a permanent Government servant at any one time without a medical certificate?
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 32, the maximum period of Extraordinary Leave (EOL) that can be granted at any one time to a permanent Government servant under normal circumstances without a medical certificate is 3 months.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, prior permission or sanction is mandatory for a Government servant to engage in which of the following activities?
Option_A: Taking part in registration, promotion, or management of any bank or cooperative society
Option_B: Undertaking honorary work of a social or charitable nature
Option_C: Participating in sports activities as an amateur
Option_D: Occasional work of literary, artistic, or scientific character
Brief_Explanation: Rule 15 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 requires prior sanction of the Government for engaging in the management of any commercial or banking company, cooperative society, or business.

Question_Text: A male Government servant with less than two surviving children is entitled to Paternity Leave for a period of 15 days. Within what period must this leave be availed?
Option_A: Within 3 months from the date of delivery of the child
Option_B: Within 6 months from the date of delivery of the child
Option_C: Within 1 year from the date of delivery of the child
Option_D: At any time within the first two years of the child's life
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 43-A, Paternity Leave of 15 days must be availed of during the confinement of the wife, i.e., up to 15 days before or up to 6 months from the date of delivery.

Question_Text: If a Government servant overstays their leave without authorization, how is the period of overstayal treated under Rule 25 of the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972?
Option_A: It is automatically condoned as extraordinary leave.
Option_B: It is debited against half pay leave due, and any excess is treated as EOL, with no leave salary paid.
Option_C: It is adjusted against earned leave at double the rate.
Option_D: It is immediately treated as dies-non for all purposes.
Brief_Explanation: Rule 25 specifies that unless the overstayal is condoned by the competent authority, the period is debited against HPL, and any excess as EOL. No leave salary is admissible for such a period.

Question_Text: As per the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, who is the authority competent to grant 'Study Leave' inside or outside India to a school staff member under the GNCTD?
Option_C: The Ministry of Education, Government of India
Option_D: The Administrator / Lieutenant Governor of Delhi
Brief_Explanation: Study Leave is a specialized leave that requires the sanction of the Administrative Ministry or the Head of Department (Director of Education) in consultation with finance.

Question_Text: Which of the following forms of communication is used in Central Government offices to communicate departmental decisions of a policy nature or to convey guidelines to subordinate offices?
Brief_Explanation: Circulars or internal instructions are used to disseminate policy-level decisions, guidelines, or structured procedural commands to subordinate offices and staff.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, a Government servant is prohibited from making any statement of fact or opinion which has the effect of an adverse criticism of any current or recent policy of the Government in which media?
Option_A: Radio broadcast or television program only
Option_B: Any document published in his own name or anonymously
Option_C: Public media, social networks, or press releases
Brief_Explanation: Rule 9 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 prohibits any adverse criticism of Government policy in any radio broadcast, television telecast, print media, document published anonymously, or social networks.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the maximum duration of Child Care Leave (CCL) that can be availed of by a single male Government servant during his entire service?
Option_D: No CCL is admissible to male employees
Brief_Explanation: The Government of India amended the rules to extend Child Care Leave (CCL) benefits to single male Government servants (unmarried, widower, or divorcee) for up to 730 days during their entire service.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, which of the following constitutes 'Insolvency'?
Option_A: Having personal loans from a registered nationalized bank
Option_B: A state of habitual indebtedness where liabilities exceed assets, rendering the employee unable to meet financial commitments
Option_C: Investing heavily in risky mutual funds
Option_D: Co-signing a loan for a family member
Brief_Explanation: Rule 17 requires a Government servant to manage their private affairs to avoid habitual indebtedness or insolvency, where their financial liabilities exceed their capacity to repay.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the rate of salary paid during the second 365 days of Child Care Leave (CCL)?
Option_D: No salary is paid during the second year of CCL
Brief_Explanation: Under the amended CCL rules, 100% of the leave salary is paid for the first 365 days of CCL, and 80% of the leave salary is paid for the next 365 days.

Question_Text: According to the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, can a Government servant accept sub-letting of Government accommodation from another Government official?
Option_A: Yes, with mutual agreement and sharing of license fee.
Option_B: No, subletting or sharing of Government accommodation without prior permission of the Directorate of Estates is strictly prohibited.
Option_C: Yes, if the other official is a close relative.
Option_D: Yes, but only for a maximum period of three months.
Brief_Explanation: Rule 15-A of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 strictly prohibits any Government servant from subletting, leasing, or otherwise sharing the accommodation allotted to him without authorized permission.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, 'Special Disability Leave' for injury intentionally inflicted or caused in the due performance of official duty is capped at a maximum of:
Option_D: No limit, for such period as is certified by an Authorized Medical Attendant
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 44, Special Disability Leave can be granted for a maximum of 24 months in respect of any one disability caused by injury inflicted in the due performance of official duty.

Question_Text: As per the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, what is the constraint on a Government servant regarding the employment of near relatives in private firms?
Option_A: They must not permit any family member to accept employment in any private firm having official dealings with their office without prior sanction.
Option_B: They cannot allow near relatives to work in any private firm whatsoever.
Option_C: They must report such employment within six months of acceptance.
Option_D: There are no restrictions on the employment of family members in private firms.
Brief_Explanation: Rule 4(1) mandates that no Government servant shall use his position to secure employment for any member of his family in any private firm. Rule 4(2) requires prior sanction if a family member accepts employment in a firm having official dealings.

Question_Text: Under CCS Leave Rules, what is the maximum number of days of Earned Leave (EL) that can be encashed at the time of availing Leave Travel Concession (LTC)?
Option_A: 5 days on each occasion, up to a maximum of 30 days in entire service
Option_B: 10 days on each occasion, up to a maximum of 60 days in entire service
Option_C: 15 days on each occasion, up to a maximum of 60 days in entire service
Option_D: 30 days on each occasion, up to a maximum of 90 days in entire service
Brief_Explanation: Rule 38-A allows a Government servant to encash Earned Leave up to 10 days at the time of availing LTC, subject to a maximum of 60 days in their entire service career.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, if a Government servant is recalled to duty from leave before its expiry, they shall be treated as:
Option_A: Still on leave until the original leave period expires
Option_B: On duty from the date on which they start their journey to join the post
Option_C: Entitled to double leave salary for the remaining period
Option_D: Eligible for compensatory leave of equal duration
Brief_Explanation: Rule 23 specifies that when a Government servant is recalled to duty before the expiry of their leave, they are treated as on duty from the date they start their journey to join the post.

Question_Text: Which rule of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 prohibits a Government servant from bringing any political or outside influence to bear upon any superior authority to further their service interests?
Brief_Explanation: Rule 20 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 strictly prohibits any Government servant from bringing political or outside influence to bear upon any superior authority to further their interest in respect of service matters.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, 'Hospital Leave' is granted to which category of Government servants?
Option_B: Non-Gazetted Government servants whose duties expose them to special risks or injuries while under medical treatment in a hospital
Option_C: Only Group 'A' officers of the Central Health Service
Option_D: School teachers during the summer vacation period only
Brief_Explanation: Rule 46 states that Hospital Leave may be granted to Group C and D (now Class III and Class IV) non-gazetted Government servants whose duties expose them to special risks or injuries.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, a Government servant is prohibited from promoting or participating in the activities of a 'Gherao' or similar coercive actions under which rule?
Brief_Explanation: Rule 7 of the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964 prohibits Government servants from engaging in or abetting any form of strike, demonstration, or coercive activity like 'Gherao'.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Leave) Rules, 1972, what is the maximum period of Earned Leave (EL) that can be accumulated at credit by school teachers (who belong to a 'Vacation Department')?
Option_D: No Earned Leave can be accumulated by Vacation Department staff
Brief_Explanation: Even though school teachers belong to a Vacation Department and get reduced EL credits, the maximum overall accumulation limit for EL remains 300 days, identical to other Government servants.

Question_Text: Under the CCS (Conduct) Rules, 1964, what is the statutory action required if a Government servant accepts a commercial employment within one year of retirement?
Option_A: They must secure the prior permission of the Government/President of India.
Option_B: They must report it to the nearest police station.
Option_C: They are exempt if they are Group 'C' employees.
Option_D: Commercial employment is completely banned for retired civil servants.
Brief_Explanation: Rule 26 of the CCS (Pension) Rules / CCS Conduct Rules requires Group A officers to obtain prior permission from the President if they accept commercial employment within one year of retirement.

Question_Text: Under the General Financial Rules (GFR) 2017, the threshold limit of estimated value of procurement of goods above which 'Advertised Tender Enquiry' (ATE) must be adopted is:
Brief_Explanation: Under GFR 2017 Rule 161, Advertised Tender Enquiry (ATE) should be the preferred method of procurement for goods valued at Rs. 25 Lakhs and above.

Question_Text: As per GFR 2017, what is the percentage of the estimated value of the contract that must be obtained as 'Performance Security' from the successful bidder?
Brief_Explanation: Under Rule 171 of GFR 2017, to ensure due performance of the contract, Performance Security is to be obtained for an amount of 5% to 10% of the value of the contract (subject to temporary Covid-era relaxations which returned to normal).

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017 Rule 170, what is the standard range of 'Bid Security' (also known as Earnest Money Deposit - EMD) that should be secured from bidders?
Option_A: 0.5% to 1% of the estimated value of the goods
Option_B: 2% to 5% of the estimated value of the goods
Option_C: 5% to 10% of the estimated value of the goods
Option_D: No bid security is required for goods below Rs. 10 Lakhs
Brief_Explanation: Rule 170 of GFR 2017 mandates that Bid Security (EMD) should range between 2% to 5% of the estimated value of the goods/services being procured.

Question_Text: According to GFR 2017 Rule 144, which of the following is a fundamental principle of public buying?
Option_A: Procuring the highest-priced brand to ensure premium quality
Option_B: Ensuring maximum efficiency, economy, and transparency, and giving fair and equitable treatment to all bidders
Option_C: Restricting the bidding process to local state-registered vendors only
Option_D: Awarding the contract to the bidder who offers the longest warranty period irrespective of cost
Brief_Explanation: Rule 144 lays down that every authority delegated with financial powers must buy public goods in a manner that ensures efficiency, economy, transparency, and equal opportunity.

Question_Text: Under the Government e-Marketplace (GeM) guidelines, up to what value can a buyer purchase goods directly from any available seller on GeM, provided they meet the requisite specifications?
Brief_Explanation: According to GFR Rule 149(i), direct online purchase on GeM up to Rs. 25,000 is permitted through any of the available sellers on GeM, satisfying quality, specification, and delivery needs.

Question_Text: Under GeM procurement, for purchases between Rs. 25,001 and Rs. 5,00,000, the buyer must select the seller offering the lowest price (L1) by comparing at least how many sellers?
Option_D: No comparison is required below Rs. 5,00,000
Brief_Explanation: Rule 149(ii) specifies that for purchases above Rs. 25,000 and up to Rs. 5,00,000, GeM purchases must be made through the seller having lowest price (L1) among at least three different OEM/sellers.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, a 'Single Tender Enquiry' (STE) is justified and can be adopted for procurement under which of the following circumstances?
Option_A: When the estimated value of procurement is less than Rs. 5 Lakhs
Option_B: When only a particular firm is the manufacturer of the required goods (proprietary items)
Option_C: When there is an urgent requirement and limited tenders will take too long
Option_D: When the local purchase committee recommends it to save shipping time
Brief_Explanation: Rule 166 of GFR 2017 permits Single Tender Enquiry (STE) only under specific conditions, primarily when the required item is proprietary (manufactured by a single source) or in times of emergency.

Question_Text: In public procurement, what is the meaning of the term 'L1'?
Option_A: The vendor who scored highest on the technical evaluation matrix
Option_B: The lowest responsive and evaluated bidder whose bid meets all technical and commercial requirements
Option_C: The local vendor situated closest to the school premises
Option_D: The bidder who submitted their bid first on the online portal
Brief_Explanation: L1 represents the Lowest Bidder (Price-wise) whose bid is responsive, compliant, and meets all criteria established in the tender document.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, which of the following is correct regarding the validity period of bids submitted by suppliers?
Option_A: Bids are valid indefinitely until a contract is signed.
Option_B: The bidding documents should specify a reasonable period of bid validity, normally ranging from 90 to 120 days.
Option_C: Bid validity cannot exceed 30 days under any circumstances.
Option_D: The validity of a bid is determined entirely by the supplier in their submission.
Brief_Explanation: GFR guidelines state that to allow sufficient time for evaluation and approval, the bid validity period must be specified clearly, normally being 90 to 120 days.

Question_Text: What is the primary purpose of the 'Two-Bid System' (Technical and Financial Bids) in public procurement under GFR Rule 163?
Option_A: To allow suppliers to quote two different prices for different quantities
Option_B: To ensure technical evaluation is completed objectively and without bias from price considerations, before opening financial quotes
Option_C: To double the paperwork and prevent audit objections
Option_D: To allow two different departments to evaluate the same bid simultaneously
Brief_Explanation: The Two-Bid System ensures that the technical specifications and capability of the bidder are evaluated objectively first. Financial bids of only those who qualify technically are opened.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, what is the maximum value of procurement of goods below which a 'Local Purchase Committee' can make purchases under Rule 155?
Brief_Explanation: Rule 155 of GFR 2017 allows purchase of goods costing above Rs. 25,000 and up to Rs. 2,50,000 on each occasion through a Local Purchase Committee.

Question_Text: Which of the following is an essential requirement for the constitution of a Local Purchase Committee under GFR Rule 155?
Option_A: It must consist of at least five members representing local business communities.
Option_B: It must consist of exactly three members of appropriate standing decided by the Head of Department.
Option_C: It must be chaired by an external auditor.
Option_D: It must include a representative from the Ministry of Finance.
Brief_Explanation: Rule 155 of GFR 2017 specifies that the Local Purchase Committee must consist of three members of appropriate standing to survey the market and recommend suppliers.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, 'Global Tender Enquiry' (GTE) should not be invited for packages having estimated value less than:
Brief_Explanation: In alignment with the 'Make in India' initiative, the Department of Expenditure amended GFR 2017 to mandate that no Global Tender Enquiry (GTE) shall be invited for tenders up to Rs. 200 Crores except with special approvals.

Question_Text: As per GFR 2017, the system of 'Limited Tender Enquiry' (LTE) can be adopted even if the estimated value exceeds Rs. 25 Lakhs under which of the following conditions?
Option_A: When the Head of Office certifies that the demand is urgent and additional advertisement delay will damage public interest.
Option_B: When there are less than ten registered suppliers in the state.
Option_C: When the purchase is funded by a private philanthropic donor.
Option_D: Limited Tender Enquiry can never be used above Rs. 25 Lakhs.
Brief_Explanation: Rule 162 specifies that LTE (up to Rs. 25 Lakhs normally) can be used for higher values if there is an urgent demand, or if the source of supply is definitely known and ATE is not in public interest.

Question_Text: Under public procurement rules, what does 'Bid Securing Declaration' refer to?
Option_A: A document where the bidder declares they have deposited cash in the bank.
Option_B: A declaration signed by bidders accepting that if they withdraw or modify their bids during validity, they will be suspended from bidding for a specified period.
Option_C: A certificate from the bank verifying the bidder's financial solvency.
Option_D: An oath taken by the bidder to maintain absolute confidentiality.
Brief_Explanation: A Bid Securing Declaration is an alternative to EMD/Bid Security where the bidder accepts suspension/debarment from bidding if they violate bidding commitments.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, 'Advance Payment' to a private firm against a contract for procurement of goods/services should not ordinarily exceed:
Option_D: No advance payment can ever be made to private firms
Brief_Explanation: Rule 172 of GFR 2017 limits ordinary advance payments to private firms to 30% of the contract value (or 40% for state-owned/maintenance contracts) to mitigate risk.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, which of the following is correct regarding the 'Liquidated Damages' (LD) clause in procurement contracts?
Option_A: It is a penalty paid to the supplier for early delivery.
Option_B: It is a pre-estimated, mutually agreed sum recovered from the supplier for delays in supply, up to a specified maximum percentage (usually 10%).
Option_C: It is a fee paid to auditors to check contract files.
Option_D: It is an insurance premium paid against damage during transit.
Brief_Explanation: Liquidated Damages (LD) represent a pre-estimated compensation deducted from the supplier's payment for delays in delivery, usually capped at 5% to 10% of the delayed goods' value.

Question_Text: Under the financial administration of the Government of India, the primary authority for checking and auditing all public accounts, receipts, and expenditures is:
Brief_Explanation: The Comptroller and Auditor General (CAG) of India, under Article 148 of the Constitution, is the supreme audit authority responsible for auditing public accounts and expenditures.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, 'Revenue Expenditure' refers to which of the following types of payments?
Option_A: Expenditure incurred on constructing a school sports complex
Option_B: Expenditure on salaries, office maintenance, utility bills, and minor repairs which do not create permanent assets
Option_C: Expenditure on buying buses for school transport
Option_D: Expenditure incurred on the first construction of a school building
Brief_Explanation: Revenue Expenditure represents recurring administrative expenses (salaries, repairs, utilities) necessary for day-to-day operations that do not result in asset creation.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, a physical verification of all consumable and non-consumable stock/inventory in a school must be conducted at least:
Brief_Explanation: Rule 213 of GFR 2017 mandates that physical verification of all fixed assets and inventory (consumable and non-consumable) must be conducted at least once a year.

Question_Text: According to GFR 2017, any loss of public money, departmental revenue, or stores due to fraud, theft, or embezzlement exceeding what threshold must be reported immediately to the CAG and the Ministry of Finance?
Brief_Explanation: Rule 33 of GFR 2017 mandates that any loss of public money/stores exceeding Rs. 10,000 due to theft, fraud, or neglect must be reported to the next higher authority, the CAG, and the Ministry of Finance.

Question_Text: Under GeM procurement, if a buyer decides to buy an item using 'Proprietary Article Certificate' (PAC) buying, what is the prerequisite?
Option_A: The PAC must be signed by the local purchase committee chairperson.
Option_B: The competent authority must certify that only one particular manufacturer's product meets their specific operational needs, justifying a single-source purchase.
Option_C: The PAC can only be used for purchases below Rs. 25,000.
Option_D: The purchase must be made using cash only.
Brief_Explanation: PAC buying on GeM allows procurement of a specific OEM's product when the competent authority signs a Proprietary Article Certificate certifying that no other brand is acceptable.

Question_Text: Under GFR 2017, 'Proprietary Article Certificate' (PAC) procurement is governed by which rule?
Brief_Explanation: Rule 166 of GFR 2017 governs single tender and proprietary article purchases (PAC buying) where specific, technical reasons justify purchasing a single proprietary brand.

Question_Text: What is the statutory role of the 'Financial Adviser' in a Central Government Department or Union Territory administration?
Option_A: To handle the accounting ledger of individual schools
Option_B: To advise the Secretary/Administrative Head on all financial, budgetary, and procurement matters, ensuring compliance with GFR
Option_C: To audit the department's tax returns
Option_D: To directly approve all expenditures without administrative consent
Brief_Explanation: The Financial Adviser (FA) is responsible for assisting the Administrative Head in maintaining budgetary discipline, evaluating purchase proposals, and ensuring GFR compliance.

Question_Text: Which of the following is correct regarding the 'Integrity Pact' under GFR procurement guidelines?
Option_A: It is an agreement where bidders pledge not to use plastic packaging.
Option_B: It is a commitment between the procuring entity and bidders to avoid any corrupt practices at any stage of the procurement process.
Option_C: It is signed only by Government-owned public sector enterprises.
Option_D: It is a declaration of assets by the procurement committee members.
Brief_Explanation: An Integrity Pact is signed in high-value public procurements (thresholds determined by ministries) binding both the buyer and bidders to avoid any collusion, bribery, or corrupt practices.

Question_Text: Under Section 12(1)(c) of the Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education (RTE) Act, 2009, private unaided schools must admit what percentage of children from weaker sections and disadvantaged groups in Class I?
Brief_Explanation: Section 12(1)(c) of the RTE Act mandates that private unaided schools must reserve at least twenty-five percent (25%) of their entry-level class seats for children belonging to weaker sections and disadvantaged groups.

Question_Text: As per the RTE Act, 2009, what is the Pupil-Teacher Ratio (PTR) prescribed for upper primary classes (Class VI to VIII)?
Brief_Explanation: The Schedule under the RTE Act, 2009 prescribes a Pupil-Teacher Ratio of 1:30 for primary classes (Class I to V) and 1:35 for upper primary classes (Class VI to VIII).

Question_Text: Under Section 13 of the RTE Act, 2009, what is the penalty if a school subjects a child to a 'screening procedure' during admission?
Option_A: Imprisonment of the Principal for up to three months
Option_B: A fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees for the first contravention
Option_C: Cancellation of the school's recognition immediately
Option_D: A token warning by the education officer
Brief_Explanation: Section 13(2)(b) specifies that if a school subjects a child to a screening procedure, it shall be punishable with a fine up to Rs. 25,000 for the first contravention and Rs. 50,000 for subsequent contraventions.

Question_Text: Under Section 17 of the RTE Act, 2009, physical punishment and mental harassment of a child are:
Option_A: Permitted only under written consent of parents
Option_B: Subject to minor warnings by the school management
Option_C: Strictly prohibited, and anyone contravening this is liable to disciplinary action under service rules
Option_D: Permitted in secondary classes for discipline
Brief_Explanation: Section 17 of the RTE Act, 2009 strictly prohibits subjecting any child to physical punishment or mental harassment. Violations attract disciplinary action under applicable service rules.

Question_Text: Which section of the RTE Act, 2009 prohibits teachers from engaging themselves in private tuition or private teaching activities?
Brief_Explanation: Section 28 of the RTE Act, 2009 mandates that no teacher shall engage themselves in private tuition or private teaching activity.

Question_Text: Under Section 21 of the POCSO Act, 2012, any person who fails to report an offence of child sexual abuse under Section 19 or 20 shall be punished with:
Option_A: Imprisonment of up to six months or fine or both
Option_B: Imprisonment of up to one year and fine
Option_C: Imprisonment of up to three years
Option_D: No criminal penalty, only department action
Brief_Explanation: Section 21(1) of the POCSO Act, 2012 states that any individual who fails to report a child sexual abuse offence shall be punished with imprisonment up to six months or fine or both.

Question_Text: Under the POCSO Rules, 2020, what is the designated role of a 'Support Person'?
Option_B: A person appointed by the Child Welfare Committee (CWC) to accompany and provide physical and psychological support to the child during legal proceedings
Option_C: A medical doctor who performs the physical exam
Option_D: A police officer in plain clothes
Brief_Explanation: A Support Person is designated under the POCSO Rules to accompany and support the child victim through the investigation, medical exam, and trial stages.

Question_Text: According to the POCSO Guidelines, what must a school principal do if they receive information that a child has been abused outside the school premises?
Option_A: Do nothing since the incident did not occur in the school.
Option_B: Report the matter immediately to the local police or Special Juvenile Police Unit (SJPU) under mandatory reporting requirements.
Option_C: Conduct an internal inquiry first and wait for parent consent.
Option_D: Advise the parents to handle the matter privately.
Brief_Explanation: Reporting under POCSO is a mandatory legal obligation. The school Principal is legally bound to report any suspected child sexual abuse to the police immediately, regardless of where the incident occurred.

Question_Text: Under the CPCR Act, 2005, which body is authorized to monitor the implementation of the Right to Education (RTE) Act, 2009?
Option_A: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
Option_B: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR)
Brief_Explanation: Section 31 of the RTE Act, 2009 delegates the responsibility of monitoring the child's right to education to the National Commission for Protection of Child Rights (NCPCR) and State Commissions (SCPCR).

Question_Text: According to the National School Safety Policy Guidelines, who should head the 'School Disaster Management Committee' (SDMC) at the institutional level?
Option_C: The President of the local Rotary Club
Brief_Explanation: At the school level, the Principal or Head of School is designated as the Chairperson of the School Disaster Management Committee (SDMC) to operationally anchor school safety.

Question_Text: Under Section 35 of the POCSO Act, 2012, the entire legal trial of a child abuse case under the Special Court must be completed, as far as possible, within a period of:
Option_A: Six months from the date of the FIR
Option_B: One year from the date of taking cognizance of the offence
Option_C: Two years from the date of the offence
Option_D: Three years from the date of filing the charge sheet
Brief_Explanation: Section 35(2) of the POCSO Act, 2012 mandates that the Special Court shall complete the trial, as far as possible, within a period of one year from the date of taking cognizance.

Question_Text: Under the RTE Act, 2009, what is the minimum number of instructional hours per academic year prescribed for Class VI to VIII (Upper Primary)?
Brief_Explanation: The RTE Act mandates a minimum of 800 instructional hours per academic year for primary classes (Classes I-V) and 1,000 instructional hours for upper primary classes (Classes VI-VIII).

Question_Text: Under the POCSO Act, 2012, if a school staff member is accused of child sexual abuse, they can be prosecuted under which specific category representing their position of authority?
Option_B: Aggravated Penetrative Sexual Assault / Aggravated Assault
Option_D: Staff members are exempt from POCSO and undergo departmental trial only
Brief_Explanation: Section 9 of the POCSO Act classifies offences committed by persons in positions of trust, authority, or control (including school teachers, management, or staff) as Aggravated Sexual Assault.

Question_Text: Under the RTE Act, 2009, no child can be subjected to which of the following actions until the completion of elementary education?
Option_A: Expulsion or holding back in any class
Brief_Explanation: Section 16 of the RTE Act (prior to the 2019 amendment relaxation of state options) laid down that no child shall be held back in any class or expelled from school until the completion of elementary education.

Question_Text: Under Section 22 of the POCSO Act, 2012, if a false complaint is filed against a child by an adult, the punishment prescribed is:
Option_B: Imprisonment which may extend to six months or fine or both
Option_C: Imprisonment which may extend to one year or fine or both
Option_D: No punishment can be given to a complainant
Brief_Explanation: Under Section 22(2), if a person makes a false complaint or provides false information against a child, they shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year or fine or both.

Question_Text: According to the RTE Rules, 2010, the local authority must maintain a record of all children in its jurisdiction from:
Brief_Explanation: Under the RTE Rules, the local authority must maintain a household registry of all children within its jurisdiction from birth to 14 years of age to ensure tracking and enrollment.

Question_Text: Under the POCSO Act, 2012, the medical examination of a child victim of sexual abuse must be conducted within what timeframe after the reporting of the offence?
Option_D: No explicit timeframe is set, but it should be done as soon as possible
Brief_Explanation: Section 27 of the POCSO Act mandates that the medical examination of a child victim must be conducted within twenty-four (24) hours of the report being received.

Question_Text: Under the RTE Act, 2009, which of the following is NOT a statutory duty of a school teacher under Section 24?
Option_A: Maintain regularity and punctuality in attending school.
Option_B: Conduct and complete the curriculum within the specified time.
Option_C: Assess the learning ability of each child and supplement additional instructions.
Option_D: Manage the financial accounting and balance sheet of the School Management Committee.
Brief_Explanation: Managing school accounts and balance sheets is the duty of the School Management Committee (SMC) or administration, not a statutory pedagogical duty of teachers under Section 24.

Question_Text: Which section of the POCSO Act, 2012 protects the identity of the child victim from public disclosure through media, newspapers, or internet?
Brief_Explanation: Section 23 of the POCSO Act strictly prohibits the media or any publisher from publishing or disclosing any details (including name, school, address, or photos) that could identify the child victim.

Question_Text: According to the National School Safety Policy, what is the role of the 'Safety Focal Point Teacher' (FPT) in a school?
Option_A: To act as the school physical instructor.
Option_B: To coordinate disaster preparedness drills, identify safety hazards, and act as a link between the school and local emergency services.
Option_C: To teach cyber safety courses only.
Brief_Explanation: The FPT is operationally responsible for anchoring all safety initiatives in the school, including structural safety audits, drills, and training.

Question_Text: Under the CPCR Act, 2005, the State Commission for Protection of Child Rights (SCPCR) consists of a Chairperson and how many members?
Option_C: Six members, of whom at least two shall be women
Brief_Explanation: Under the CPCR Act, the SCPCR consists of a Chairperson and six members appointed by the State Government, with a statutory requirement that at least two members must be women.

Question_Text: Under the RTE Act, 2009, the minimum academic year requirement for Class I to V is:
Brief_Explanation: The Schedule under the RTE Act prescribes a minimum of 200 working days for primary classes (Classes I-V) and 220 working days for upper primary classes (Classes VI-VIII).

Question_Text: Under the POCSO Guidelines, if a child reports an incident of abuse to a teacher, the teacher should:
Option_A: Advise the child to keep it a secret to prevent defamation.
Option_B: Listen empathetically, validate the child's feelings, and immediately inform the School Principal for mandatory police reporting.
Option_C: Contact the suspect directly to clarify the issue.
Option_D: Reprimand the child for talking about inappropriate topics.
Brief_Explanation: Teachers must provide a supportive environment for children disclosing abuse and are legally required to report the disclosure to the Principal/police immediately.

Question_Text: Under Section 31(3) of the CPCR Act, 2005, which authority can be constituted by the State Government in districts where SCPCR has not yet been established?
Option_B: A temporary child rights commission or designated local authority
Option_C: A designated Civil Court to act as a Child Rights tribunal
Brief_Explanation: Section 31(3) permits the State Government to constitute temporary authorities or designate existing authorities to perform SCPCR duties pending its formal setup.

Question_Text: According to the school infrastructure standards in the RTE Act, 2009, which of the following is a mandatory structural facility?
Option_B: A barrier-free play area with ramp access
Option_D: A dedicated auditorium with 500+ seating capacity
Brief_Explanation: The RTE Schedule mandates that every school building must be barrier-free to ensure inclusive access for children with physical disabilities, alongside a playground.

Question_Text: Under NEP 2020, what is the target year by which 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in school education (from pre-school to secondary level) must be achieved?
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 sets a target of 2030 to achieve 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in school education, spanning pre-school to Grade 12.

Question_Text: The national standard-setting assessment body 'PARAKH' proposed under NEP 2020 will function under which organization?
Brief_Explanation: PARAKH (Performance Assessment, Review, and Analysis of Knowledge for Holistic Development) is set up as a standard-setting body and national assessment center under NCERT.

Question_Text: Which of the following digital platforms is designated as the 'National Digital Infrastructure for Teachers' under the Ministry of Education?
Brief_Explanation: DIKSHA (Digital Infrastructure for Knowledge Sharing) acts as the national digital repository and platform for school teachers to access e-learning, lesson plans, and training.

Question_Text: What does the digital program 'PM e-VIDYA' offer to school children across India?
Option_A: Free laptops to all high school students
Option_B: Multi-mode access to digital/online education, including 12 dedicated DTH TV channels (one class, one channel) and radio broadcasts
Option_C: A scholarship scheme for digital literacy courses
Option_D: High-speed internet installation in rural schools
Brief_Explanation: PM e-VIDYA is a comprehensive initiative unifying digital, on-air, and online educational resources, notable for its 12 class-specific educational DTH channels.

Question_Text: As per the NEP 2020, what is the minimum duration of professional training (B.Ed. degree) that will be required to become a teacher by the year 2030?
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 specifies that by 2030, the minimum degree qualification for teaching will be a 4-year integrated B.Ed. degree, focusing on holistic, multidisciplinary training.

Question_Text: Under digital education initiatives, what does 'NISHTHA' stand for?
Option_A: National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement
Option_B: National Institute for Secondary and Higher Teacher Holistic Assessment
Option_C: National Integrated Scheme for Holistic and Technological Advancement
Option_D: National Initiative for Student Health and Training in Holistic Arts
Brief_Explanation: NISHTHA stands for National Initiative for School Heads' and Teachers' Holistic Advancement, which is the world's largest integrated teacher training program.

Question_Text: Which national portal serves as a repository for free NCERT textbooks, audios, videos, and interactive learning materials for students, teachers, and parents?
Brief_Explanation: ePathshala is a joint digital platform developed by MoE and NCERT that hosts textbooks, audiovisual resources, and digital resources for free public access.

Question_Text: Under NEP 2020, the vocational education curriculum must be integrated starting from which grade?
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 recommends that vocational exposure and education must be integrated into the school curriculum starting from Grade 6 (Middle Stage), including a 10-day bagless period.

Question_Text: Under digital education guidelines, what is the role of NCERT's 'Translation Cell'?
Option_A: To translate foreign literature into English
Option_B: To translate national digital textbooks and e-learning resources into scheduled Indian languages to promote mother-tongue education
Option_C: To handle administrative letters in Hindi only
Option_D: To translate CBSE curriculum into international languages
Option_D_Explanation: The translation cell specializes in regional language availability, not international curriculum export.
Brief_Explanation: The translation cell of NCERT is specifically tasked with translating textbooks, e-content, and study materials into Scheduled languages to support regional education.

Question_Text: Which organization has been designated as the National Coordinator for managing SWAYAM courses for school-level education?
Brief_Explanation: NCERT is the designated National Coordinator for school education SWAYAM MOOCs, while NIOS handles out-of-school children, and NPTEL handles engineering.

Question_Text: Under NEP 2020, what is the proposed structure of the 'Gender Inclusion Fund'?
Option_A: A fund to build separate hostels for girls only
Option_B: A fund to provide sanitary pads in schools
Option_C: A central fund dedicated to providing equitable quality education for all girls as well as transgender students
Option_D: A scholarship scheme for women teachers
Brief_Explanation: The Gender Inclusion Fund is proposed to ensure states have resources to support equitable education, safe infrastructure, and sanitation for girls and transgender students.

Question_Text: According to the NEP 2020, what is the target Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) for higher education, including vocational education, to be achieved by 2035?
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 aims to increase the Gross Enrolment Ratio in higher education, including vocational education, from 26.3% (2018) to 50% by 2035.

Question_Text: Which AI-driven initiative is being integrated under digital school education portals to offer students personalized, adaptive learning paths?
Option_C: Automated biometrics for student attendance only
Option_D: Generative chat assistants for school admins
Brief_Explanation: National digital infrastructure projects are focusing on integrating Personalized Adaptive Learning (PAL) using AI to assess student needs and dynamically adjust lessons.

Question_Text: Under NEP 2020, what is the 'State School Standards Authority' (SSSA) responsible for?
Option_B: Regulating and establishing minimum common standards for both public and private schools in a State/UT
Brief_Explanation: SSSA is an independent state-level body proposed to regulate and monitor minimal quality and administrative standards across all public, private, and philanthropic schools.

Question_Text: What does NEP 2020 recommend regarding the 'Medium of Instruction' in schools?
Option_A: English must be the compulsory medium of instruction from Grade I.
Option_B: Wherever possible, the medium of instruction until at least Grade 5, but preferably till Grade 8 and beyond, should be the home language/mother tongue/local language.
Option_C: Sanskrit must be the primary medium of instruction in all public schools.
Option_D: The medium of instruction is decided by the CBSE board only.
Brief_Explanation: NEP 2020 strongly emphasizes promoting multilingualism, recommending the home language/mother tongue as the medium of instruction wherever possible, up to Grade 5 or 8.

Question_Text: Which digital initiative acts as an online portal designed specifically for tracking student learning outcomes and enabling data-driven governance across schools?
Brief_Explanation: The Shagun portal (from 'Shala' and 'Gunvatta') is a web-based platform launched by the Ministry of Education to monitor and track the progress of school schemes and outcomes.

Question_Text: Under the school complex model recommended by NEP 2020, what is the main objective of grouping schools?
Option_A: To close down smaller primary schools to save costs
Option_B: To share vital resources (like ICT labs, libraries, sports facilities, music/art teachers) and improve academic governance in a 5-10 km radius
Option_C: To standardise the salary of teachers
Option_D: To merge boys' and girls' schools into co-educational campuses
Brief_Explanation: School complexes group a secondary school (hub) with primary and middle schools (spokes) to facilitate resource sharing, peer collaboration, and better governance.

Question_Text: Under digital platforms, what is 'Swayam Prabha'?
Option_A: A personal laptop scheme for girls
Option_B: A group of 34 (now expanded to 40) high-quality DTH educational channels broadcasting educational programs 24/7
Option_C: An AI chatbot for answering syllabus doubts
Brief_Explanation: Swayam Prabha is an educational initiative utilizing GSAT-15 satellite to broadcast high-quality educational programs on DTH TV channels 24/7.

Question_Text: Under NEP 2020, what is the target year for universalizing secondary school education with 100% GER?
Brief_Explanation: The policy targets complete universalization of school education (Grades 1-12) with 100% Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) by the year 2030.

Question_Text: What does the abbreviation 'DIET' stand for in teacher education and support frameworks?
Option_A: Department of Institutional Education and Training
Option_B: District Institute of Education and Training
Brief_Explanation: DIET stands for District Institute of Education and Training, which is a district-level Government agency responsible for organizing teacher training and curriculum support.

Question_Text: An achievement test with a reliability coefficient of 0.60 is doubled in length. Applying the Spearman-Brown Prophecy formula, what is the new reliability coefficient?
Brief_Explanation: Spearman-Brown Formula: r_new = (n * r_old) / (1 + (n - 1) * r_old). Here, n = 2 (doubled), r_old = 0.60. Calculating: (2 * 0.60) / (1 + 1 * 0.60) = 1.20 / 1.60 = 0.75.

Question_Text: Which measurement scale is characterized by classifications, ranks, and equal intervals, but lacks a true absolute zero point?
Brief_Explanation: The Interval Scale possesses classifications, ranks, and equal intervals but has an arbitrary zero point (e.g., Temperature, IQ scores), meaning ratio operations are not permitted.

Question_Text: If a distribution of test marks is highly skewed with a few exceptionally high scores, which measure of Central Tendency is most affected and pulled upward?
Brief_Explanation: The arithmetic mean utilizes every single value in a dataset, making it highly sensitive to extreme outliers or skewed distributions, whereas median and mode remain relatively stable.

Question_Text: In a standard normal distribution curve (symmetric and bell-shaped), what is the relationship between the Mean, Median, and Mode?
Brief_Explanation: In a perfectly symmetric normal distribution curve, the Mean, Median, and Mode coincide perfectly at the center point of the distribution.

Question_Text: Which type of evaluation is specifically designed to assess entry behavior, prerequisites, and placement of students before starting a new instructional sequence?
Brief_Explanation: Placement Evaluation is conducted prior to instruction to determine a learner's entry behavior, pre-requisite skills, and suitable placement in a course.

Question_Text: The psychometric property representing the degree to which a test measures what it claims or is designed to measure is known as:
Brief_Explanation: Validity refers to the extent to which an instrument or test accurately measures the specific attribute or construct it was designed to evaluate.

Question_Text: Which statistical test is most appropriate to analyze if there is a significant difference between the means of two independent groups of students on an achievement test?
Brief_Explanation: The Student's t-test is a parametric statistical test used to compare the means of two independent groups of observations to determine if they differ significantly.

Question_Text: Under a standard normal distribution curve, approximately what percentage of all observations falls within the range of Mean +/- 2 Standard Deviations (M +/- 2\u03c3)?
Brief_Explanation: In a normal curve, approximately 68.26% of values fall within Mean +/- 1 SD, 95.44% fall within Mean +/- 2 SD, and 99.73% fall within Mean +/- 3 SD.

Question_Text: The Thurstone scale of attitude measurement is commonly referred to as the:
Brief_Explanation: L.L. Thurstone's method of attitude measurement is known as the Method of Equal-Appearing Intervals (Likert's scale is the Method of Summated Ratings).

Question_Text: A standard score (Z-score) is calculated using which mathematical formula?
Brief_Explanation: The standard score Z represents the number of standard deviations an individual raw score X is above or below the Mean: Z = (X - Mean) / SD.

Question_Text: If a test has a reliability of 0.50, and we want to increase its reliability to 0.75, how many times must we increase the length of the test? (Use Spearman-Brown prophecy formula)
In educational measurement, which type of reliability is determined by administering the identical test to the same group of students after a short time interval?
Brief_Explanation: Test-Retest Reliability evaluates the stability of test scores over time by administering the same test to the same group twice with an intervening time gap.

Question_Text: Which type of scale consists of arbitrary numbers assigned to classify or label mutually exclusive categories without any quantitative order or value?
Brief_Explanation: The Nominal Scale is the simplest level of measurement, used only for labeling or classifying categories (e.g., Jersey numbers, gender classification).

Question_Text: In Bloom's Taxonomy of cognitive objectives, which level represents the ability to judge the value of material, ideas, or methods for a given purpose?
Brief_Explanation: In Bloom's original cognitive taxonomy, 'Evaluation' is the highest level, requiring judgements of value based on internal and external criteria.

Question_Text: Which of the following is an example of a 'non-parametric' statistical test?
Brief_Explanation: Parametric tests (t-test, ANOVA) assume normal distribution. Non-parametric tests like Chi-Square make no distributional assumptions and are used for nominal/ordinal data.

Question_Text: In a derangement problem involving 4 envelopes addressed to 4 teachers, what is the probability that NO envelope reaches the correct teacher?
Brief_Explanation: The number of ways to derange 4 elements is D_4 = 9. The total permutations of 4 elements is 4! = 24. Hence, the probability is 9/24 (which simplifies to 3/8).

Question_Text: An item analysis reveals that a test question was answered correctly by 90% of the students. What is the 'difficulty index' (p-value) of this item?
Brief_Explanation: The difficulty index (p) is the proportion of examinees answering correctly. A value of 0.90 indicates that 90% got it right, classifying it as an extremely easy item.

Question_Text: The 'Standard Error of Measurement' (SEM) of a test score is mathematically calculated as:
Brief_Explanation: The Standard Error of Measurement (SEM) represents the standard deviation of error scores: SEM = SD * sqrt(1 - r), where r is the reliability coefficient.

Question_Text: Which type of validity is assessed by correlating scores on a newly constructed test with an established criterion measure obtained at a future date?
Brief_Explanation: Predictive Validity is a type of criterion validity where the test scores are used to predict performance on a criterion measure administered in the future.

Question_Text: A researcher is studying the effect of three different teaching methods on the test scores of students. Which statistical technique should be used to compare the means of these three groups?
Brief_Explanation: To compare the means of three or more independent groups simultaneously on a continuous dependent variable, Analysis of Variance (ANOVA) is the standard parametric technique.
